The 2025 Indian Premier League was the 18th edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), a professional Twenty20 (T20) cricket league held in India, organized by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI). It has been held annually since the first edition in 2008.[1] In July 2024, the IPL Governing Council held a meeting with the owners of the franchises and announced that a mega auction would be conducted ahead of the 2025 season.[2] It was the sixth mega auction after 2008, 2011, 2014, 2018 and 2022.[3][4]

The franchises were required to submit their retention lists before 31 October 2024, and a total of 46 players were retained ahead of the auction. The auction was held on 24 and 25 November 2024 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with the auction purse for each franchise set at ₹120 crore (US$12 million), the highest in the history of the IPL. A total of 1,574 players registered for the auction, of which 574 players were shortlisted to feature in the auction and 182 were sold in the auction. Rishabh Pant became the most expensive player in the history of IPL when he was bought by the Lucknow Super Giants for ₹27 crore (US$2.8 million),[5] surpassing ₹26.75 crore (US$2.8 million) paid by the Punjab Kings for Shreyas Iyer earlier in the same auction,[6] and ₹24.75 crore (US$2.6 million) paid by the Kolkata Knight Riders for Mitchell Starc in the 2024 auction.[7] Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest player sold in the IPL history at the age of 13 years, being bought by the Rajasthan Royals for ₹1.1 crore (US$110,000).[8]

Following the IPL's suspension and rescheduling, it was announced that the franchises were allowed to sign temporary replacement players in place of unavailable players as the rescheduled fixtures clashed with the international cricket calendar, notably the West Indies' tour of Ireland, the West Indies' tour of England and the World Test Championship final.[9] These temporary replacement players were not available for retention in the 2026 auction.[10][11]

Player retention

[edit | edit source]

Retention policy

[edit | edit source]

The ten franchises were allowed to retain a maximum of six players each from their squad, the highest number allowed before any of the mega auctions. The six players could consist of a maximum of five capped players (including Indian and overseas players) and two uncapped players.[15] The auction purse for each franchise was set at ₹120 crore (US$12 million), the highest in the history of the IPL.[16] Franchises were deducted a specific amount from the auction purse for every retained player. Franchises who did not retain the maximum number of players were allowed Right-to-Match (RTM) cards at the auction.[17]

Auction

[edit | edit source]

Any player willing to play in the IPL was required to register for the auction. Players who did not register for the mega auction would become ineligible to participate in the mini-auctions held in subsequent years.[30] Any auctioned player withdrawing before the season without legitimate reason or injury would be banned from the IPL for a period of two years.[31] Any Indian capped player who had not been named in the starting XI in international cricket (Test, ODI, T20I) in the preceding five calendar years or did not have a central contract with the BCCI was considered as an uncapped player for the auction.[32][33][34] The salary cap of a player would consist of auction purse, incremental performance pay and match fees. Each playing member (including the impact player) would get a match fee of ₹7.5 lakh (US$7,800) in addition to the auctioned price.[35]

The auction was held on 24 and 25 November 2024 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.[36] Mallika Sagar was appointed as the auctioneer for the second consecutive time after she hosted the 2024 auction.[37][38] A total of 1,574 players registered for the auction,[39] of which 574 players were shortlisted to feature in the auction.[40]

Sold players

[edit | edit source]

Two sets of marquee players went up for bidding first followed by 15 sets of players divided based on their specialisation: batters, all-rounders, wicket keeper batters, fast bowlers and spin bowlers; and status: capped and uncapped. After player no. 116, the auction entered its accelerated phase, covering all the remaining players. During the accelerated round, players were presented based on the franchises' preference.[42][43]
